# Capability matrix

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask capabilities` from manifest.toml and the tagged tests. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every operation of the [feature inventory](../research/pdf/06-feature-inventory.md#3-full-operation-inventory-with-mechanisms) (06 §3), with the best status a passing test proves on each surface ([full-editor §3](../plans/full-editor.md#3-tracking-the-capability-matrix)). Rows, IDs and target rounds are in [`manifest.toml`](manifest.toml); a status appears here only when a tagged test proves it.

**Statuses**, weakest first: 🔴 `unsupported` (detected and reported, never silently dropped), 🟡 `read` (displayed or extracted faithfully), 🔵 `write` (created or changed; output passes qpdf `--check` and opens in pdf.js and PDFium), 🟢 `round-trip` (open → change → save → reopen preserves the feature and everything else). `—` means no evidence yet; `n/a` means the row doesn't target that surface. **Columns:** `core` (the Rust crates), `pdf` (`@laminapdf/sdk`), `web`, `desktop`; *Target* is the round that must reach the target status on every targeted surface.

**Evidence.** A Rust test claims a status with a doc-comment line above it, `/// capability: C.08 core round-trip` (ID, surface, status; several lines for several claims), on a `#[test]` function in a crate's `src/` or `tests/<name>.rs`. A TypeScript test claims one at the start of its title, `it("[cap J.01 web round-trip] edits the title, …")` (several tags in a row for several claims), on a plain `it(` or `test(` call (not `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo`, `.skipIf` or `.runIf`), only in the TypeScript library's Node tests (`packages/sdk/test/*.test.ts`, the `pdf` column), the reader's end-to-end tests (`apps/web/e2e/*.e2e.test.ts`, the `web` column) and the desktop app's scenarios (`apps/desktop/e2e/specs/*.e2e.ts`, the `desktop` column). `cargo xtask capabilities` runs every tagged Rust test and rewrites this page and [`matrix.json`](matrix.json) (the same matrix as data, which the reader's capability page shows); it doesn't run the TypeScript tests, which need the WebAssembly build or the built apps: the fast lane's `WASM` job runs the library's, `cargo xtask pdf-runtimes` runs the reader's in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in the fast lane, and the full lane's `desktop-e2e` jobs run the desktop's on Linux, macOS and Windows; a pull request must pass both lanes' gates to merge. `cargo xtask capabilities --check` (full lane) fails when this page or `matrix.json` differs from what the passing tests prove or a tagged Rust test fails, and `cargo xtask check docs` (every PR, no test run) fails when this page claims more than any tagged test could prove or either file differs from what the manifest and the tags generate. Core `write` and `round-trip` may be claimed only by tests in the round-trip suite ([`roundtrip_suite.rs`](../../crates/laminapdf-save/tests/roundtrip_suite.rs)), whose saves the full lane's `cargo xtask roundtrip` also checks with qpdf `--check`, pdf.js and PDFium.
